newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - J Matthey sees mixed H1 progress.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - J Matthey sees mixed H1 progress.

text.p: Johnson Matthey, the precious metals and industrial materials company, said good growth in electronics and a recovery in catalytic systems powered a nine percent rise in first-half pre-tax profits but other sectors were subdued.

Gordon Thorburn, executive director for administration, told Reuters that the 15 percent increase in profits from electronic materials reflected a strong performance by subsidiary Advance Circuits Inc, acquired last year.

"We have also made good progress with our plastic laminate packages project. That will make some money in the second half and is the principal reason for us being quite enthusiastic about our prospects for next year in that division," he said.

But the precious metals and ceramics sectors remain subdued. "Precious metals will be flat, but it is a very sound business and ceramics is in good shape but needs to wait on tile markets in particular to recover," Thorburn said.

Overall pre-tax profits rose to 51.2 million stg, led by growth in the electronic materials division, up 15 percent and in catalytic systems, up 22 percent. Shares were up 11-1/2p at 545-1/2 by 1010 GMT.
Thorburn said the microelectronics market was generally difficult. "Sales are actually down in that market in the current year, so we're pleased with our progress there."
The catalytic systems division was boosted by healthy world car markets.
"But in ceramics the markets have been getting quite difficult with the depression in the German construction industry, which affects the tile industry," Thorburn said.
He expected strong demand in electronics to continue into the second half. "That varies, but in microprocessors in particular there is very strong demand," he said.
"Memory chips, for which we supply high purity titanium, also will recover in time. That has been the principal reason for difficulties in electronics markets."

Thorburn said the company saw opportunities for growth in Asia. "Asia generally is major part of our growth strategy. It won't produce immediate benefits but there are steady improvements," he said, adding that there were good prospects for ceramics there and in Brazil.
